from gateway.idempotency import IdempotencyStore


def test_replayed_key_does_not_re_execute():
    store = IdempotencyStore()
    calls = {"n": 0}

    def handler():
        calls["n"] += 1
        return f"result-{calls['n']}"

    first = store.execute_or_replay("k1", handler)
    second = store.execute_or_replay("k1", handler)
    assert calls["n"] == 1
    assert first == "result-1"
    assert second == "result-1"
explanation: Replays the same key twice with a counting handler and asserts the handler ran once and the cached response was returned on replay. No existing test replays a key, which is why removing the cache-hit short-circuit survived.
rationale: Asserting the handler is invoked exactly once across two calls with the same key detects the missing replay-suppression guard.
